notes.title: V1.0.0 — She's Alive. God Help Us All.
notes.description: After mass migrations, duplicate purges, column name existential crises, and enough SQL debugging to qualify as a form of therapy — Emergent Energy Dashboard V1 is officially real. We built an entire renewable energy project management platform. The sun rises, the panels generate, and the dashboard finally loads without a 500 error. Mostly.

notes.title: The Great Light Theme Reformation
notes.description: The entire app was reborn in glorious white and Emergent green (#16A34A). The dark theme has been exiled, banished, sent to live on a farm upstate. Every pixel now sparkles with the energy of a freshly cleaned solar panel. Your retinas may need a moment to adjust. We recommend sunglasses.

notes.title: Project Command Center: Now With 73% Less Scrolling
notes.description: The project detail page got a full makeover. The header went from 'corporate PowerPoint circa 2019' to 'clean command center you'd actually want to look at.' Six overview cards were ruthlessly compressed into a compact tabbed layout because apparently people have things to do other than scroll. Plan, Engineering, Quality, Finance, Collaboration, and PD — all one click away. Revolutionary concept: fitting information on one screen.

notes.title: Permission Gating: Your Access Has Been Denied (Politely)
notes.description: We built an entire permission system so that not everyone can see everything anymore. Sidebar items now vanish like your motivation on a Monday if you don't have the right role. Try to sneak in via URL? Access Denied page. Beautiful, clean, and deeply unsympathetic. We mapped 30+ routes to permission entities. Some of you will log in and wonder where half the sidebar went. That's not a bug. That's governance.

notes.title: Universal Search: It Actually Searches Now
notes.description: The search bar on the home page used to be decorative. A beautiful, non-functional input field — like a chocolate teapot. It now searches across projects, tasks, cost lines, and revenue lines in real time. The SQL JOIN that powered it was using a column that didn't exist (project_info_id as a primary key — narrator: it was just called 'id'). Fixed. You're welcome.

notes.title: The Great Duplicate Purge of 2026
notes.description: We discovered 2,105 duplicate work items living rent-free in the database. The backfill script was creating new records every time it ran instead of updating existing ones. It was like a copy machine that nobody turned off. We deleted them all and added deduplication logic. The database lost weight. It feels lighter. It's been doing yoga.

notes.title: Task Deletion: Now Deletes Tasks
notes.description: Plan tasks without a rowNumber were being silently skipped when you tried to delete them. The button worked, the confirmation appeared, the loading spinner spun — and absolutely nothing happened. The task would stare back at you, undeletable, eternal. We added a direct database delete endpoint for these rogue tasks. They can now be sent to the shadow realm as intended.

notes.title: Cashflow Endpoint: No Longer Crashes The Universe
notes.description: The /api/cashflow endpoint existed in two places simultaneously — routes.ts AND finance-routes.ts — like a project manager double-booked in meetings. One had a safety guard requiring a project filter. The other did not. Guess which one Express picked? Without the guard, it tried to load every cashflow point, every expense, every inflow, every operational task, and every project plan simultaneously. Stack overflow. Maximum call stack size exceeded. The server briefly contemplated the meaning of existence before giving up. Fixed with six lines of code.

notes.title: Revenue Tab: Now Speaks Bearer Token
notes.description: The Revenue tab's API calls were going out without authentication headers, like showing up to a black-tie event in pyjamas. Every fetch got a 401 Unauthorized. We gave them their Bearer tokens. They're dressed appropriately now. The PLANNED column was also removed because it contained no data and existed purely to make the table wider.

notes.title: Capture Deliverable: Because Email Attachments Are Not A Filing System
notes.description: You can now capture project deliverables directly from the Collaboration tab. Upload documents, assign them to team members, categorise them by type. It's everything your shared drive folder named 'FINAL_FINAL_v3_ACTUALLY_FINAL' wished it could be.

notes.title: Roles & Permissions Grid: Compact Edition
notes.description: The permissions page went from a scrollable novel to a compact grid with single-letter action toggles. V, C, E, D — View, Create, Edit, Delete. It's like a board game but for access control. Bulk-set entire categories with one click. Your scroll wheel has been formally laid off.

notes.title: 63 Projects. 4,500+ Cost Lines. 361 Inflows. One Dashboard.
notes.description: This thing manages actual renewable energy projects with actual money. Total contract revenue across the portfolio: R263 million. Gross profit margin: 17%. We computed these numbers live from canonical tables with pure-function modules because we are professionals. The KPIs update in real time. The charts use Recharts. The data is real. None of this is mocked. We repeat: none of this is mocked.

notes.title: Easter Egg Status Update
notes.description: Still there. Still undiscovered. It's starting to develop abandonment issues. If you find it, it will be genuinely surprised. It had given up hope. Please look for it. It's lonely.
